---
title: "Starting a blog!"
format: html
---

Scientific papers are great and all, being the agreed upon way to make science at the moment, but they can’t be the only outlet for scientific debate. For one thing, post-publication discussion is often severely lacking (or post-publication peer review, if you want to make a big deal of it). Sure, some people might talk about it at a conference, and nobody else will know; or make an off-handed comment while referencing it, with the readers of the original paper none the wiser; response articles exist, but you don’t want to go through peer review unless it’s something really big, and it seems more of a way to get into an academic fight than anything. 
I’m not ashamed to say that I have learnt more from some posts on blogs such as those in [resources](/resources.qmd). Inspired by those and others, I decided to start a blog, in the hope of doing a bit of the same myself. I will share some ideas that I think are useful, without having to be so formal, and with the possibility for anyone involved to have a discussion in real time, as allowed by the internet.
